paragraphs.text: Since his childhood, the male claimant has had a life of problems because of his gypsy origins. His children were dismissed by their teacher because they are gypsies. Around XXXX XXXX, 2007, when some individuals were threatening his brother, the male claimant was attacked and injured in the mouth by individuals because he wanted to call the police.
Following this attack, the male claimant was hospitalized and wanted to file a complaint with the police, but they refused to accept the complaint.
After his hospitalization, the male claimant received a hospital bill of 28,000 kunas; however, as he was unable to pay it, he was imprisoned for a period of four months.
On XXXX XXXX XXXX 2011, some individuals tried to rape his spouse.

Around XXXX XXXX, 2011, the male claimant was beaten by Croats who told him that he did not have the right to buy bread. The male claimant tried to file a complaint, but the police did nothing. Around XXXX XXXX, 2011, the male claimant was struck by some individuals who threatened to set fire to his wife and children.
Before coming to Canada, some Croats told the male claimant that Hitler should have killed all the gypsies.
He also alleged that his wife was abused and threatened by some individuals who had set upon her while she was gathering empty bottles to sell in order to feed his children.

In his reply to question 31 of his Personal Information Form (PIF),4 the male claimant states that he was injured by some individuals around XXXX XXXX, 2007, when he tried to help his brother. When asked by his counsel where he was coming from when he saw his brother being attacked, the male claimant replied, [translation] "From XXXX," adding that he had gathered scrap metal in XXXX and that he was returning to his home.

Moreover, when confronted with his reply to question 41 of his refugee protection claim form,7 which indicates "I have not experienced persecution in my life," the male claimant stated [translation] "I never was. But, I had to flee because I could no longer take the abuse. The children came from school; they had pulled their hair. Now, life is respected. Unfortunately, if the children are taken out of school. I may be illiterate, but at school we are rejected because of our nationality. I decided to really leave. I am prepared to be imprisoned in Canada as I am not badly treated. If I must return there, at 13 or 14 years old, they no longer have the right to go to school. I do not want them to be illiterate like me because they can no longer go to school. I have experienced many things in my life, but I do not want my children to experience the same things, and this is why I asked for help from Canada."
